title: 3.5.12 Lab: Build a Small Nested-Object Structure
description: Build an object with a nested object and an array of objects, then read values out of it. Auto-graded.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([Start]) --> B[make the order, with a customer object and an items array]
  B --> C[/print the customer name/]
  C --> D{more items left}
  D -- yes --> E[/print this items name and price/]
  E --> D
  D -- no --> F([End])

steps.title: Outer object
steps.instructions: Create a variable for it (the lesson calls it order; use any name that fits what you are building) and assign it an object literal.

steps.title: Nested object
steps.instructions: Give the order a customer property whose value is another object with at least a name field.

steps.title: Array of objects
steps.instructions: Give the order an items property whose value is an array of at least two objects, each with a name and a price.

steps.title: Read the nested object
steps.instructions: Print the customer's name using a chain: the order, a dot, customer, a dot, name.

steps.title: Walk the array and read each field
steps.instructions: Loop over the items array and print each item's name and price using bracket index then dot field.

requirements.title: nested object built
requirements.description: order holds another object: written inside its braces, assigned with a dot, or built first and placed in. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: One of the order's properties must itself be an object: put a second pair of braces inside the first.

requirements.title: array of objects built
requirements.description: An array holds objects: written in the brackets, pushed in, or built first and listed. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Give the order an items property that is an array whose elements are objects, each in its own braces.

requirements.title: customer chain read
requirements.description: console.log prints a field of the customer reached with a chain (order.customer.name), or a variable holding that read or holding order.customer. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Chain the dots one step at a time and print the result: console.log(order.customer.name). order.items.length is a different chain, and a read on a line of its own prints nothing.

requirements.title: index then field read
requirements.description: console.log prints a field read off one item: order.items[i].name, or the item held in a variable (a loop variable, a forEach parameter, or const item = order.items[i]) then a dot. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Pick one item with its index in square brackets, then read a field off it with a dot, inside console.log: console.log(order.items[i].name). A helper that returns the text, printed from the loop, counts too: that is checked when you press Run.

requirements.title: loop prints each item
requirements.description: A loop over the items (for, for...of, while or forEach, on order.items, a variable holding it, or counting to the number of items) prints a field read off each item, itself or through a helper function it calls. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))
requirements.hint: Loop over order.items and, inside the loop, print the current item's name and price read with a dot (order.items[i].name), not fixed text. A helper the loop calls that prints or returns the line counts too (checked on Run).

requirements.title: order holds a customer object and a list of items
requirements.description: After the code runs, order.customer is an object with a name, and order.items is an array of at least two objects, each with a name and a price. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Build order with a customer object (with a name) and an items array holding at least two objects, each with a name and a price.

checks.fail: order should be an object literal: const order = { ... }.

checks.expr: order.customer !== null && typeof order.customer === 'object' && Object.values(order.customer).some(v => typeof v === 'string')
checks.fail: order.customer should be an object with a name in it (text in quotes), like customer: { name: "Marisol" }. You may call the field anything that fits.

checks.expr: Array.isArray(order.items) && order.items.length >= 2 && order.items.every(i => i !== null && typeof i === 'object')
checks.fail: order.items should be an array holding at least two objects, one per item.

checks.expr: order.items.every(i => Object.values(i).some(v => typeof v === 'string') && Object.values(i).some(v => typeof v === 'number'))
checks.fail: Every item needs some text (its name, in quotes) and a number (its price, with no quotes around it). You may call the fields anything that fits.

requirements.title: the customer name and every item are printed by reads that run
requirements.description: Code that runs prints the customer name read from order, and a loop prints every item's name and price, one item per line. A printed undefined names the read that found nothing. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Print order.customer.name, then loop over order.items and print the current item's name and price inside the loop.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line says undefined: a read found nothing. Check the spelling of each name you read.
The customer's name is not printed by code that runs. Print it with the chain, console.log(order.customer.name), on a line that runs.
Not every item's name and price is printed from the loop. Loop over order.items and, inside the loop, print the current item's name and price read with a dot.

checks.expr: (() => { const S = (x) => Object.values(x).find(v => typeof v === 'string'); return order.items.every(i => output.some(l => l.includes(S(i)) && order.items.every(o => o === i || S(i).includes(S(o)) || !l.includes(S(o))))); })()
checks.fail: Two items are printed on the same line. Print one item per line, from inside the loop, instead of one line that lists them all.
